title: Bound the result inside the tool
lesson: A tool's response shape decides what lands in the agent's context: a raw read_logs dump looks fine on a quiet service, floods the context during the incident so the useful line is truncated away, and a bounded search_logs(service, window, limit) moves the filtering into the tool and returns the few lines and IDs the agent needs.
limitations: Illustrative scenario: the truncation point, the line counts and the agent's '?' answer are an example. A real agent may answer confidently and wrongly after truncation, which is worse and is not shown; truncation limits differ by harness.
A bounded tool reduces what reaches the context; it does not guarantee the incident is found or that the returned lines are the right ones. Evaluate on recorded runs.
Limits must be enforced in the tool's implementation. Tool descriptions, prompt instructions and persistent system prompts do not enforce limits, pagination or permissions.
Pagination cursors, coverage fields and the empty-versus-failed distinction are not shown; the baseline cut covers empty versus failed.

Final audio was checked through decoded peak (-1.8 dBFS), cue-window signal and spectrograms, not listening. The author's earlier onset check is historical; the comparative review does not claim frame-exact perceived synchronization.
A small returned log sample does not establish absence of incidents; the opening reports only the received line count. Pagination and coverage still require an explicit contract.
transcript: 0:01–0:06 — Normal case. The agent asks read_logs for web over a one-hour window. Logs returns 12 lines; three representative dots land and the context bar fills a little. The agent displays the neutral receipt '12 lines read', making no claim that there were no incidents.

0:08–0:12 — The incident. The agent asks the same tool about 'payments'. Logs works longer and returns 3,214 lines; the raw lines stream to the agent and the context bar fills to a rising scale, turning orange.

0:13.7–0:15.1 — Overflow. The context bar turns red and a TRUNCATED badge appears. Later lines are dropped with red crosses, including INC-42 at about 14.4 seconds. In this scripted example the agent then displays '?'; this is not a guarantee of uncertainty after truncation.
0:18–0:19 — Redesign. The tool is relabelled from read_logs to search_logs with service, window and limit. At about 19 seconds the context bar drains and the badge disappears.

0:20–0:25.2 — Resolution. The agent asks search_logs for payments, one hour, limit 20. The tool sends a filter request to Logs, which returns 3 lines. A green INC-42 chip reaches the agent at about 24.4 seconds with a small context footprint; the displayed answer becomes INC-42 at about 25.2 seconds.
0:28.4–0:29.6 — The stage fades to the dark background while the title remains, returning to the opening title-only frame.

changes: Replace unsupported 0 incidents conclusion after 12 log lines with neutral 12 lines read.
Declare the already-requested window in read_logs inputs; enlarge input labels.
Move redesign ripple clear of tool labels.
Cap local FFmpeg input, output and filter threads at two.
Publication polish: paraphrase source excerpts with claim links; clarify scripted uncertainty and transcript phase timing; scope audio metadata to final measurements.
originalTranscript: 0:01–0:05 — Normal case. The agent asks read_logs for the quiet 'web' service over the last hour. Logs returns 12 lines; three dots land on the agent, its context bar fills a little, and the agent answers '0 incidents' in green.

0:08–0:12 — The incident. The agent asks the same tool about 'payments'. Logs works longer and returns 3,214 lines; the raw lines stream to the agent and the context bar fills to a rising scale, turning orange.
0:14 — Overflow. The bar snaps red, jolts, and a TRUNCATED badge pops up. Later lines are dropped at the agent with red crosses, including the one green chip, INC-42. The agent can only answer '?'.
0:18 — Redesign. The tool is relabelled in place from read_logs to search_logs with service, window and limit; the context bar drains and the badge disappears.

0:20–0:25 — Resolution. The agent asks search_logs for payments, one hour, limit 20. Logs does the filtering itself, returns 3 lines, and a single green INC-42 chip reaches the agent. The bar fills only slightly, in green, and the agent answers 'INC-42' with a chime.
0:28 — The stage fades to black under the title so the video loops cleanly.
